findings.reason: each proposed mechanism's milestone should be restated as "extend <owner>" against the file that already implements it, and M1's premise ("impl is a settable scalar the server does not auto-compute") is factually obsolete on section-record plans.
findings.text: §3.3/M3 records the archive sweep as "automated sweep still pending", but `run_archive_pass` (invoked by `reckon archive --project P --older-than-days N --apply`, reckon/cli.py:8159) already implements exactly that policy: `find_archive_candidates` selects done/superseded docs older than the threshold and `apply_archive_candidates` sets `plan-archived=1` (reckon/archive.py:61,112). The plan builds rather than cites. Other unlisted-existing mechanisms: §3.1's impl invariant already exists — `_store.py:2384` refuses an author-set `impl` on a section-record plan and derives it via `_plan_html.py:678 derive_impl_from_sections`; §3.1's write-time-refusal-with-audit-severity shape already exists in `reckon/mcp.py:1903 _unwired_plan_refusal` + `reckon/_schema.py:320 unwired_plan_message` + `reckon/roadmap.py:1009 _unwired_plan_findings`; §3.3's "dashboard default view shows ONLY live docs" is already the SPA default (`docs/ui/shell.jsx:339` filters archived; `reckon/serve.py:2216 include_archived=False`); §3.4's pre-flight "does an existing plan own this lifecycle?" already exists as `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md:299` step 3 ("Search existing plan and research titles/summaries before creating a new resource").

findings.reason: the plan should extend the section-derived mechanism rather than add a parallel impl-guard, or state why the owner cannot cover the shipped-with-zero-impl case.
findings.text: §3.1 proposes a write-time invariant forcing `impl` to be set with status→shipped/done, but the impl-set rule already has an owner: `_store.py:2384` (via `_plan_html.py:678 derive_impl_from_sections`) computes `impl` from section records and refuses a direct set with a naming error ("impl is computed from the section records on this plan … It is not authorable — move a section's status instead"). A second invariant beside this one forks the rule.

findings.reason: the plan must target `_close_sprint_with_carry_forward` as the extension point and reconcile its predicate with the item-held predicate already enforced there, or the two close gates will disagree.
findings.text: §3.5 proposes a sprint-close gate via "reckon-edit close-sprint intent", but sprint-close already has a live owner and a live closability refusal: `_close_sprint_with_carry_forward` refuses to close a sprint with incomplete, unheld items and carries held work forward. The gate the plan wants (unresolved followups / unset impl / uncollapsed sections) is a different predicate on the same close path, so it must be added there — and the plan names the wrong owner (reckon-edit, not the project-state close path).

findings.reason: naming one owning module (and the invariants it exports) collapses six shallow, separately-gated milestones into one deep surface and stops each mechanism from re-deciding what "finished" means.
findings.text: the plan scatters one concept (finished work must be recorded finished) across §3.1 (server write-time), §3.2 (CLI audit + schedule), §3.3 (archive + dashboard), §3.4 (skill pre-flight), §3.5 (close path), §3.6 (fleet backfill) with no module named to own the invariants; a `reckon/lifecycle.py` ("Derived lifecycle state for plans and sprint items") and `reckon/doccheck.py:491 audit_lifecycle` already exist and would be the single home that hides the section-record, status and followup rules behind one interface.

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend the existing Step 3 pre-flight into a checkable gate, not add a parallel prompt.
findings.text: §3.4 adds a pre-flight question to `reckon-create`, a thin layer over the existing pre-flight search at SKILL.md:299 (step 3 already tells the author to search existing plan/research titles before creating). The plan does not say why that search cannot simply be strengthened or made refusing (e.g. surfaced as a roadmap/audit finding, matching the `unwired-plan` precedent) rather than wrapper-ed as a new conversational prompt a worker may skip.

findings.reason: the section must account for its added refusal/warning surface in its own text — naming what it supersedes or stating why the existing `unwired-plan`-style channel cannot carry these invariants.
findings.text: §3.1's "reject-on-write" branch and §3.5's "refuses to close" both add to the refusal family, and §3.1's "auto-set with warning" branch adds to the warning family, yet §3 gives no sentence naming what these retire or merge. The neighbouring precedent shows what is missing: `unwired_plan_message` (reckon/_schema.py:320) shipped its invariant as one message + one audit finding with a severity ramp, retiring no surface but stating so.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the plan has no single owner for lifecycle invariants: one concept (a plan that is finished must be recorded finished) is spread as six milestones across five enforcement sites over the same audit/refusal machinery, with no module named to hide the spread.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — three of the plan's mechanisms duplicate infrastructure with a live owner: the impl-set rule, the sprint-close gate, and the archive sweep.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §3.1 (reject-on-write) and §3.5 (refuse-to-close) each add enforcement surface to the refusal/warning family and neither names what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes four mechanisms that already exist in reckon (archive sweep, impl-set invariant, write-time refusal-with-audit-severity, plan-creation pre-flight search) and cites none of them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3.4 adds a pre-flight question to `reckon-create` on top of the existing title/summary search without saying why that search cannot be extended.
